To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the faecal excretion pattern of porphyrin isomers is characteristic for all the seven common types (hepatic or erythropoeitic) of human porphyrias.

the proportions of the four faecal coproporphyin isomers I—IV are altered in all types of human porphyrias, and that the isomer pattern is a reliable diagnostic and differential diagnostic tool in human porphyrias.

in the porphyrias: (a) isomer I is increased in erythropoiesis, (b) isomers II, III and IV are increased in hepatic porphyria, (c) isomer III is increased in coproporphyrias, (d) isomer IV is increased in coproroporphyrias, (e) isomer I to III ratios are increased in erythropoeitic porphyrias, and (f) isomer II to III ratios
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new, reliable and reproducible method for the determination of faecal coproprophyrin I- IV in human porphyrias.
the development and evaluation of a new method for the quantitative determination of faecal copporphyrin isomers in porphyrias, and with the diagnostic significance of these findings.
the development and application of a reliable method for the determination of the four copporphyrin isomers in faeces.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the isomer pattern of faecal copropphorphyrin is characteristic for each type of porphyria, and that the isomer patterns are diagnostic for each type of hereditary porphyrin, with the exception of porphobilinogin synthase deficiency porphyrin and protoporphyric porphyria.
the faecal copro III/I ratio is the single most important marker in the differential diagnosis of the porphyrias.

faecal copropyrin isomer ratios may help to distinguish the various types of porphyria from each other, but cannot be regarded as a reliable diagnostic tool to distinguish the various forms of porphyria.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

faecal coproporphyin I-IV ratios are of great value for the diagnosis of hereditary coproporphyrins and variegate porphryias and that faecal coprorporphyrin III/I ratios are useful in the diagnosis of acute hepatic porphyrins and in the identification of carriers of the gene defect in hereditary coproprophyrin.

the determination of faecal copporphyrin I-III-IV isomer patterns in patients with acute hepatic porphyrins and erythropoietin porphyrias is of great importance for differential diagnosis and the identification of the underlying enzyme defect.
in the porphyrias the isomer pattern of the faecal porphyrin metabolites reflects the type and site of porphyrin biosynthesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that

faecal coproporphyin I-IV ratios are an important tool in the differential diagnosis of the porphyrias, and can be used to identify asymptomatic carriers of the gene defect in families of patients with hereditary coporphyria.
the faecal excretion pattern of coproporphyrins I—IV is an extremely sensitive diagnostic tool for the differential diagnosis of heredytary porphyrias.
the isomer pattern of faecal coprorporphyrins is a valuable tool for the diagnosis of porphyrias.
